Exhibition simulator

Exhibition simulator

Version 3.78

Business case

An exhibition you can walk through before it exists.

Until now, presenting an exhibition before it exists has meant building it twice: first in InDesign, designing every panel, and then again in Photoshop, manually placing those designs onto photographs and adjusting scale, perspective and shadows. Every small change meant repeating the process. Meanwhile, physical layouts, dimensions and distances were often estimated on site, making it extremely time-consuming to create a reliable preview of the final result.

  1. Visualise before you build

    Create a full-scale digital model of the exhibition space, using the actual dimensions of the panels, showcases and other elements. Experiment with layouts, move elements around and test different configurations before anything is built.

    Preview your panel designs with real content, without the repetitive InDesign-to-Photoshop workflow. With augmented reality, you can even place the entire exhibition in the actual room, at full scale. Everyone can see the proportions, understand the space and make decisions with confidence.

  2. Decide before you produce

    Test compositions, hierarchy, dimensions and readability before anything is printed or installed.

    Stand where the visitor stands, see the exhibition at eye level and measure the exact distance from which a text will be read. No more guesswork or printed tests to check dimensions and readability on site.

    Generate updated views and presentations as the layout changes, and share them with management, technicians and production teams.

  3. Collaborate from the start

    Editors can add their text directly to the panels at full scale, see how it fits and edit it themselves, without relying on a designer for every adjustment. Instead of going through several rounds of drafts to make content fit, editors can deliver text that is already adapted to the physical space.

How it works

  1. Build the row. In Composition, set how many panels or showcases you want, then click each position to choose its type: M and L are frames of two widths, V is a showcase on legs.
  2. Arrange it. In Layout selection, pick straight, curved, accordion or facing, set the spacing, and move the sliders each layout adds. Builder mode lets you drag the panels around instead.
  3. Add content. In Panels content, upload a picture for each plate, or tick Show demo text to put a sample page at real size on every panel. Open panel editor to write on the panels themselves: start from a layout, then add, move and resize titles, text, quotes, captions and pictures, and see where the text runs past its box. See it in 3D takes you back to the room, in front of that panel.
  4. Look around. Drag to orbit, shift-drag or the arrow keys to pan, scroll to zoom; Overview, Front and Top jump to set views. The reading distance at the bottom measures from the camera to the cross in the middle of the view, so you can tell whether a text size works from where you are standing.
  5. Take it away. Augmented Reality mode opens the composition at real size on an iPhone or iPad, and Export PNG saves the view you are looking at.

Showcase sets the size of the display case. Light and shadow moves the light and softens the shadow. Everything is drawn in millimetres at real size.
